scenario: An xfs mount whose mountinfo super options carry the kernel-emitted token usrquota (accounting plus enforcement on) and no noquota, probed at the mount point itself and at a nested directory below it.

fixture.mountinfo:
29 25 0:30 /@root / rw,relatime shared:1 - btrfs /dev/mapper/root rw,compress=zstd:3,ssd,discard=async,space_cache=v2,subvolid=257,subvol=/@root
31 29 259:2 / /srv/xfsquota rw,relatime shared:7 - xfs /dev/nvme0n1p2 rw,attr2,inode64,logbufs=8,logbsize=32k,usrquota

rationale: CORRECTED CASE (round-23 pre-seal amendment, .ufo/waves/round-23/preseal-amendment.md, written before any candidate implementation was opened or measured; no C2 result observed). Same id and same scenario as the proposal cases-proposed/CaseXfsUsrquota.json, which is retained unaltered as the original proposal. Delta versus the proposal is exactly one fixture member: the single btrfs_sysfs UUID record (a decoy for the btrfs root line) gains the amendment-required member qgroups_enabled, set to null because the record's qgroups is false, which the amendment pairs explicitly ('qgroups false must pair with enabled=null/mode=null'; the record already carries qgroups_mode null). The amendment also states that a btrfs_sysfs UUID record must have exact bool/bool-or-null/mode-or-null types for the qgroups fields and that missing or extra record keys are a setup error, so the record's key set is exactly devices, qgroups, qgroups_enabled, qgroups_mode. Every other part of the fixture (mountinfo text, both paths entries, device_links) and every expected value are unchanged from the proposal. Re-derivation against the amendment's superseding C2 rules leaves the expectation identical, because this case is an XFS case and no amended rule changes the XFS usrquota outcome: (1) Mount resolution — the amendment keeps longest component-prefix selection and adds 'if ANY covering mountpoint occurs more than once, refuse classification as unknown/n/a/ambiguous_overmount, fstype=null, mount_point=null, device_check=not_checked'. The fixture's two mount points are '/' (the btrfs root line) and '/srv/xfsquota' (the xfs line), each occurring exactly once, so no covering mountpoint is duplicated and the ambiguity rule cannot fire. For realpath /srv/xfsquota the mount point '/srv/xfsquota' qualifies by equality (and the root '/' qualifies as '/'); for realpath /srv/xfsquota/projects/data it qualifies because the realpath starts with '/srv/xfsquota/'. The longest covering mount point is '/srv/xfsquota' in both cases, so the chosen line is '31 29 259:2 / /srv/xfsquota rw,relatime shared:7 - xfs /dev/nvme0n1p2 rw,attr2,inode64,logbufs=8,logbsize=32k,usrquota', whose last three fields after the separator are fstype xfs, source /dev/nvme0n1p2 and the super options string. The amendment's rule to parse the separator and the last three fields of each chosen line (never file-wide) yields the same result here, and no backslash escape occurs in the line, so the octal-decoding rule (040/011/012/134 only) is not engaged. (2) Device check — the amendment states that a device mismatch PREEMPTS the filesystem table (unknown/n/a/device_mismatch, device_check=mismatch), and that the btrfs equality skip applies only when the stat major is 0. Here the chosen fstype is xfs (not btrfs) and the mount major:minor 259:2 equals the paths' st_dev 259:2, so no mismatch is declared and the XFS table is reached. Anchor: proc.rst section 3.5 (S082) line 1975, 'major:minor: value of st_dev for files on filesystem'. (3) XFS precedence — the amendment's ordered XFS precedence is 'conflict (noquota with ANY quota/enforcement or noenforce key), then noquota, then any enforced key, then any accounting-only key, else absent'. The fixture's super options split on commas into keys rw, attr2, inode64, logbufs, logbsize, usrquota: there is no noquota, so neither the conflict branch nor the noquota branch applies; usrquota is an enforced key, so the third branch applies and yields quota_state enabled, enforcement enforced, basis xfs_quota_option. The other branches are unreachable (no accounting-only-only key set, no absent state). The mixed enforced/noenforce clarification ('SOME quota-type enforcement flag is set, not all') does not apply because only one quota key is present. The amendment's quota_option_keys content rule (noquota and recognized xfs keys only, sorted) is a supplementary output check outside this case's six-field scored tuple. (4) Kernel meaning of the token — S078 (fs/xfs/xfs_super.c v7.2, xfs_fs_show_options lines 238-241) prints ',usrquota' exactly when mp->m_qflags & XFS_UQUOTA_ENFD is set and ',uqnoenforce' when only XFS_UQUOTA_ACCT is set, and lines 253-254 print ',noquota' only when no quota accounting flag is set; so a kernel-emitted usrquota token with no noquota is exactly the enforced state, which is what the enforced cell records. S077 (Documentation/admin-guide/xfs.rst v7.2) supplies the option vocabulary: noquota at 171-173, uquota/usrquota/uqnoenforce/quota at 175-177, gquota/grpquota/gqnoenforce at 179-181, pquota/prjquota/pqnoenforce at 183-185. (5) Verdict precedence — the amendment keeps the precedence 'setup error, else any enabled -> 1 QUOTA_ENABLED, else any unknown -> 2 QUOTA_STATE_UNKNOWN, else 0 QUOTA_DISABLED' and stresses that positive evidence is never hidden by an unknown sibling; both probed paths are enabled, so the run verdict is exit 1 with finding_id QUOTA_ENABLED. (6) Fixture hygiene under the amendment — both paths are nonempty, unique, normalized absolute paths with no dot or dotdot components, and st_dev 259:2 is a canonical decimal MAJ:MIN with no sign and no leading zero; the UUID key 8f3c1a2e-5b47-4d19-9c08-7e6b2a4d9f13 is canonical; the devices entry and the device_links mapped value are plain nonempty basenames without slashes. The fixture's btrfs root line is a decoy only: it is never the chosen mount for either probed path (longest component prefix wins), so the amended btrfs rules (qgroups presence meaning INITIALIZED, enabled true/false/null, the btrfs_qgroups_enabled / btrfs_qgroups_disabled / btrfs_qgroups_enabled_unavailable bases) are unreachable for this case, and the decoy's own record shape (qgroups false with enabled null and mode null) is the amendment-mandated pairing for an absent qgroups directory. Recorded ambiguity for L1, unchanged from the proposal and not resolved here: the token enforced records the filesystem-level enforcement flag (XFS_UQUOTA_ENFD set, hence the emitted token per S078), not the existence of any per-user or per-group limit or an armed EDQUOT; S077's wording 'limits (optionally) enforced' shows the option names do not assert that a limit exists, and the contract's limits paragraph concedes that no per-user/group/project limit or usage is read, so no other token is available.
